description:
## Goal

Delete the unused Enumerable slicing scaffold rather than grow public `Enum.slice` surface. There is no public caller; the only direct protocol calls are scaffold fixtures.

## Why deletion is correct

The old expansion commit `2f2855ce` adds 165 Enum lines and roughly 36 definitions to rescue dead code. Its `Enumerable.slice/1` result erases incompatible Map and Range callback shapes as `any`; Enum then reconstructs receiver-specific dispatch and impossible-state repairs, creating a second authority and overlapping fz-5xp.85. It also exposes the known composed-stride bug in the current Range callback, while its fixture omits the source-step plus slice-step case.

Deletion removes work, unreachable maintenance surface, erased callback shape, protocol implementations, and two deterministic Range specialization rungs without losing a demanded capability.

## Scope

Delete `Enumerable.slice/1`, all list/map/range implementations, `Map.slice/1`, `Range.slice/6`, `Range.slice_from/5`, and now-unused `Range.reverse/2`; remove slice-only protocol fixtures/assertions and stale census prose; preserve any independent sparse-callable regression without claiming Map.slice is its production motivation. Re-measure deterministic work after deletion.

Update fz-5xp.82 to omit slicing until a real demand exists. Keep fz-5xp.108 and fz-kdt.117; their reduced witnesses are independent.

## Acceptance

- No maintained source calls or declares `Enumerable.slice` / `Enum.slice` / `Map.slice` / `Range.slice`.
- The deleted callback shape has no reconstruction, fallback, or compatibility residue.
- Focused protocol/range/fixture tests, deterministic rung/work evidence, formatting, and strict checks prove the smaller result.
- PR #139 is replaced by this deletion work; do not replay its expansion commit.

comments.text: Decision: finish the existing slicing scaffold. Enumerable.slice/1 is the protocol callback that should power public Enum.slice/2,3; the names do not conflict because they belong to different modules. This ticket will add the consumer and remove slice/2,3 from fz-5xp.82 rather than delete the optimized Map and Range paths.

Completed in 008a1e1f0. Added public Enum.slice/2 and slice/3 with direct list traversal, the existing unary Map slicing callback, the existing ternary Range slicing callback, and a generic Enumerable.to_list fallback. Negative indexes are normalized after counting; zero amounts and empty or out-of-bounds windows return an empty list; negative amounts and nonpositive range steps abort. The oracle fixture covers lists, maps, ranges, positive and negative bounds, empty input, out-of-bounds starts, zero amounts, and overshooting strides on all three execution doors. Evidence: 724/724 fixture legs; 2020 compiler library tests passed with 6 ignored; 260/260 runtime; 30/30 CLI; workspace doctests; AOT variadic-open; clippy with warnings denied; fmt; diff check. Review also produced fz-5xp.108 for incorrect runtime clause selection when a guard reads a destructured struct field. The known direct-only callable transport limitation remains owned by fz-kdt.117; these protocol callbacks are consumed in the receiver-specific clause rather than transported through a helper.

title: Delete unused Enumerable slicing scaffold
